s: Seafront castle above Mirbat’s old port and market · seat of the wali
dr: A castle at Mirbat was recorded in 1884; rebuilt under Sultan Said bin Taimur
el: Rectangular plan with two defensive towers, two floors
te: The castle above the old harbour
se: On the eastern edge of Mirbat, a two-tower castle looks down on the old port and the traditional market
sa: على الطرف الشرقي من مرباط يطلّ حصن ذو برجين على الميناء القديم والسوق التقليدي
desc: A castle on the eastern side of Mirbat, Dhofar, overlooking the old seaport (al-Furda) and the traditional Mirbat market. The Ministry of Heritage and Tourism notes that no precise date for the original building is known; the British writer Miles reported a castle there after visiting Mirbat in 1884, and the present building was rebuilt during the reign of Sultan Said bin Taimur. It has a rectangular plan with two main entrances and two defensive towers on two floors: the ground floor held servants’ rooms, soldiers’ quarters, an arms store, a prison and a kitchen, and the upper floor four residential rooms including a majlis for the wali’s family. It is open to visitors.
sig: The administrative and defensive heart of historic Mirbat, one of Dhofar’s old trading ports.
ex: Ministry of Heritage and Tourism (Experience Oman)
disc: Overlooks the old port of al-Furda
refs: Ministry of Heritage and Tourism. Mirbat Castle. Experience Oman. https://experienceoman.om/destinations/dhofar/mirbat-castle
conf: Coordinates are the centre of the map bounding box embedded on the Ministry’s Experience Oman page (≈100 m); the 1884 mention is the earliest date given, so the timeline starts there

s: Early 20th-century residence of Taqah’s sheikh and wali · now a museum
dr: Built in the reign of Sultan Taimur bin Faisal (1913–1932); renovated 1991, museum from 1994
te: The governor’s home by the sea
se: In the fishing town of Taqah, a stone castle with three watchtowers shows how a Dhofari governor lived
sa: في بلدة طاقة الساحلية يكشف حصن حجري بثلاثة أبراج مراقبة كيف كان يعيش والٍ في ظفار
desc: A two-storey stone building in Taqah, Dhofar, built as the residence of Sheikh Ali bin Timman Al Ma’shani during the reign of Sultan Taimur bin Faisal (1913–1932). In the 1960s an outer wall and three defensive watchtowers were added to protect the wali, who used it as his private residence until 1984. The ground floor has a reception hall (barza), a guard room, a weapons store and a prison; the upper floor held the wali’s family quarters. It was renovated in 1991 and reopened as a museum in 1994.
sig: A well-preserved example of a 20th-century Dhofari governor’s residence and administrative centre.
refs: Archnet. Taqah Castle (Husn Taqah). https://next.archnet.org/sites/22155
conf: Coordinates from the Archnet map marker; about 1.9 km from the existing Salalah khawrs point but a separate historic building; Archnet’s style-period year 1744 is not explained and is not used

s: Abandoned coastal village with shell midden and 200-tomb cemetery · eastern Dhofar
dr: Surface pottery dates the ruins to the 17th century or later
el: Village of about 3–5 ha; cemetery of about 200 tombs
se: On a terrace above a silted wadi mouth, stone houses, a tiny mosque and a huge pile of shells mark an old fishing village
sa: على مصطبة فوق مصبّ وادٍ طمرته الرواسب، تدلّ بيوت حجرية ومسجد صغير وكومة هائلة من الأصداف على قرية صيد قديمة
desc: A coastal site about 200 km north-east of Salalah, on a terrace about 5 m above a small silted wadi estuary near Hasik. It comprises a village of roughly 3–5 ha with stone houses, single-room storehouses and a square mosque about 5 × 5 m with a mihrab in its west wall, a large shell midden, and a cemetery about 200 m to the north with roughly 200 tombs marked by plain upright stelae. Surface finds include iron tools, glass bangles, Bahla ware, blue-and-white porcelain, stoneware and green-glazed ware, which date the ruins to the 17th century or later. The site was surveyed by the University of Naples L’Orientale mission.
sig: A rare recorded late Islamic fishing settlement on the remote eastern Dhofar coast.
refs: Giunta, R. & Pavan, A. (2022). First Archaeological Activities by the University of Naples L’Orientale in Dhofar, Sultanate of Oman. Archeologia tra Oriente e Occidente 1. https://unora.unior.it/bitstream/11574/216023/1/Giunta_Pavan%20First%20archaeological%20activities%202022.pdf
conf: Coordinates are the published village point (17°23′53.1″N 55°17′22.5″E); the paper also lists 55°17′42.5″E for the village. The end of occupation is not dated, so t1 (about 1900) is a broad estimate. Arabic name: حاسك is established; القديمة translates ‘Qadim’

s: Walled promontory settlement above Salalah’s port · pre-Islamic and medieval
dr: Two occupation phases; few sherds suggest late pre-Islamic then medieval occupation
el: Promontory site about 42 m wide and 75 m north–south
se: High on a rocky cape west of Salalah, old stone walls once watched for fish, ships and enemies
sa: على رأس صخري غرب صلالة كانت أسوار حجرية قديمة ترقب أسراب السمك والسفن والأعداء
desc: A promontory site at Raysut, west of Salalah, overlooking the modern Salalah port and now enclosed by a modern wall; the surveyed area is about 42 m wide and 75 m north–south. Phillips (1972) described a defensive wall on the west and south sides and dwellings of semi-dressed stone on bedrock, similar to the older walls of Al Baleed. Brief excavations by the American Foundation for the Study of Man identified two occupation phases, and Newton and Zarins (2017) reported two cemeteries of boat-shaped graves and a fortified headland settlement comparable to Khor Rori. The few sherds collected in the 2022 survey suggest a late pre-Islamic occupation followed by a medieval one.
sig: One of the fortified coastal sites of ancient Dhofar, linked by building technique to Al Baleed and Sumhuram.
refs: Giunta, R. & Pavan, A. (2022). First Archaeological Activities by the University of Naples L’Orientale in Dhofar, Sultanate of Oman. Archeologia tra Oriente e Occidente 1. https://unora.unior.it/bitstream/11574/216023/1/Giunta_Pavan%20First%20archaeological%20activities%202022.pdf
conf: Coordinates are the published point (16°56′02.3″N 54°00′30.3″E). The site is not firmly dated; the timeline (about AD 200 to AD 1500) is a broad estimate for ‘late pre-Islamic then medieval’. Arabic name is a descriptive rendering (ريسوت is established)

s: Monsoon-fed karst spring building mossy tufa cliffs · Jebel Qara near Taqah
dr: Tufa deposits from intermittent karst springs; not dated
el: Tufa walls with bulbous forms and stalactites
se: Above Taqah, spring water rich in lime trickles down a cliff and slowly turns into new rock
sa: فوق طاقة يتساقط ماء نبع غني بالكلس على جرف صخري ويتحوّل ببطء إلى صخر جديد
desc: A waterfall at Khasur in the Taqah area of Dhofar, formed where intermittent, lime-rich karst springs emerge from the limestone of the Qara mountains. As the water flows over the cliff it deposits tufa, building walls with the typical bulbous forms of tufa and some stalactites. The walls stay wet and mossy, especially after the summer monsoon (khareef). The site is freely accessible.
sig: An accessible example of the active tufa deposition that shapes Dhofar’s monsoon springs.
refs: Duckeck, J. Ayn Athum Waterfall (شلالات عين اثوم), Oman. Showcaves.com. https://showcaves.com/english/om/karst/AynAthum.html
conf: Coordinates from Showcaves.com; timeline is a broad Quaternary estimate because the tufa is not dated; the link to the khareef is general Dhofar context

s: Tufa-walled gorge and plunge pool below the Qara escarpment · rimstone dams like Plitvice
dr: Rimstone pools, tufa deposits and a tufa cave; not dated
el: Gorge about 170 m long; reported discharge 42 l/s
se: North of Salalah, spring water has built its own stone dams and walls along a 170 m gorge
sa: شمال صلالة بنى ماء الينابيع سدوده وجدرانه الحجرية بنفسه على امتداد خانق طوله 170 مترًا
desc: A spring site at the foot of the Qara hills north of Salalah, reached by following the valley upstream from Itin Street. Karst water feeds an intermittent wadi in which precipitated limestone forms dams and pools; when the river is dry the pools become terraces and the dams vertical tufa walls. A gorge about 170 m long with tufa walls on both sides leads to a waterfall with a plunge pool and a small tufa cave, and a second tufa waterfall at Ittin lies about 800 m upstream. One source reports a discharge of 42 l/s.
sig: Shows how karst springs on the Dhofar escarpment build rimstone dams and tufa walls.
refs: Duckeck, J. Ayn Jarziz (شلال جرزيز), Oman. Showcaves.com. https://showcaves.com/english/om/karst/AynJarziz.html
conf: Coordinates from Showcaves.com; the discharge figure comes from an unnamed source cited there; timeline is a broad Quaternary estimate because the tufa is not dated

s: Small solution cave under an old river conglomerate · Wadi Halfayn, Izki
dr: Cave dissolved below a calcite-cemented conglomerate; formation has stopped
el: Triangular passage with flat ceiling and V-shaped walls
te: The cave under the river stones
se: Below the ruins of Al Nazar near Izki, a short cave hides under a roof made of old river pebbles
sa: تحت أطلال قرية النزار قرب إزكي يختبئ كهف قصير تحت سقف من حصى نهر قديم
desc: A small horizontal karst cave in Wilayat Izki, Ad Dakhiliyah, below the ruins of Al Nazar village in the normally dry Wadi Halfayn. It is cut in soft, fine-grained white limestone; its nearly horizontal ceiling is a conglomerate of rounded rubble cemented by calcite and capped by clay. The single, fairly straight passage has a triangular profile with a flat ceiling and V-shaped walls and ends after a few metres. Showcaves.com interprets it as dissolution of the limestone after the wadi cut deeper and drained the groundwater below the conglomerate; cave formation has since stopped. The name Jarnan is given as the pre-Islamic name of Izki.
sig: A compact record of river erosion, cementation and later dissolution in the interior foothills.
refs: Duckeck, J. Jarnan Cave (كهف جرنان), Oman. Showcaves.com. https://showcaves.com/english/om/caves/Jarnan.html
conf: Coordinates from Showcaves.com; the formation history is the page author’s interpretation; timeline is a broad Quaternary estimate because the cave is not dated

s: Limestone gorge with turquoise pools and a waterfall inside a cave · near Tiwi
dr: Gorge cut by flash floods; cave waterfall formed by fallen blocks
te: The secret waterfall in the cave
se: Walk and swim up a gorge of pale cliffs to find a waterfall hidden inside a cave
sa: امشِ واسبح في خانق بين جروف شاحبة لتصل إلى شلال يختبئ داخل كهف
desc: A gorge in the Ash Sharqiyah South Governorate, entered from the coast near Tiwi village about 170 km from Muscat. Sculpted limestone cliffs enclose a chain of clear turquoise pools, and the gorge is deepened by floodwater after heavy rain. About 45 minutes’ walk upstream, visitors swim through a narrow opening to a waterfall inside a cave, formed where rocks fell from the walls above. Access begins with a short boat crossing at the wadi mouth.
sig: One of the best-known limestone gorges of the eastern Hajar coast.
ex: Showcaves.com; Ministry of Heritage and Tourism (Experience Oman)
refs: Duckeck, J. Wadi Shab, Oman. Showcaves.com. https://showcaves.com/english/om/gorges/WadiShab.html
Ministry of Heritage and Tourism. Wadi Shab. Experience Oman. https://experienceoman.om/destinations/al-sharqiyah-south/wadi-shab
conf: Coordinates from Showcaves.com; timeline is a broad Quaternary estimate because the gorge is not dated

s: Window into Oman’s oldest crust · Tonian arc rocks about 880–830 million years old
dr: Gneiss protolith 884 ± 4 Ma; granodiorite 836 ± 4 Ma; cooling about 830 Ma
te: The oldest rocks of the east
se: South of Sur, granite and gneiss show a slice of crust made in a volcanic arc almost 900 million years ago
sa: جنوب صور تكشف صخور الجرانيت والنايس شريحة من قشرة تكوّنت في قوس بركاني قبل نحو 900 مليون عام
desc: Jebel Ja’alan, about 50 km south of Sur and 15 km north of Jalan Bani Bu Ali, exposes Precambrian basement mapped over an area of about 2 × 3.5 km. Ten rock units were mapped, including the Al Wafi Schist, Ja’alan Gneiss, Ja’alan Granite and Kamil Granodiorite, cut by dolerite and andesite dykes. Zircon U–Pb dating gave 884 ± 4 Ma for the gneiss protolith and 836 ± 4 Ma for the granodiorite, with monazite in the schist recording metamorphism at 834 ± 12 Ma and muscovite cooling at about 830 Ma. Peak conditions of about 650–700 °C at 4–7.5 kbar and juvenile isotope signatures point to a volcanic-arc setting.
sig: Among the oldest dated rocks in Oman, possibly the leading edge of India’s Neoproterozoic accretionary margin.
refs: Alessio, B.L., Blades, M.L., Murray, G., Thorpe, B., Collins, A.S., Kelsey, D.E., Foden, J., Payne, J., Al-Khirbash, S. & Jourdan, F. (2017). Origin and tectonic evolution of the NE basement of Oman: a window into the Neoproterozoic accretionary growth of India? Geological Magazine. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0016756817000061
conf: Coordinates converted from published sample JA15-08 (UTM 40N, 742899 E, 2460099 N, WGS84); journal name inferred from the DOI. About 2 km from the existing Jabal Qahwan Nature Reserve point, which is an ecology record; this record covers the basement geology

s: Four-towered 17th-century fort on a plateau above Sur
dr: Attributed to Imam Nasir bin Murshid Al-Ya’rubi (first half of 17th century) or to the Portuguese; taken by Omanis in 1648; restored 1989
el: About 2,500 m², walls about 55 m long and over 5 m high
se: From a rocky plateau, Sunaysilah’s round and square towers once watched the coast and the road into Sur
sa: من فوق هضبة صخرية كانت أبراج السنيسلة المستديرة والمربعة ترقب الساحل والطريق إلى صور
desc: A fort on a high rocky plateau south of the village of Sunaysilah in Sur, Ash Sharqiyah South. The Ministry of Heritage and Tourism reports two accounts of its origin: construction ordered by Imam Nasir bin Murshid Al-Ya’rubi in the first half of the 17th century, or an earlier Portuguese fort watching the coast, the Wadi Al-Fulaij estuary and the inland road, captured by Omanis under Sultan bin Saif in 1648. It covers about 2,500 m², with walls about 55 m long and over 5 m high and four towers, three circular and one square, built to withstand cannon fire. Inside are a mosque with two mihrabs, a Qur’an classroom, a prison, a barzah hall, stores and a water reservoir; it was last restored in 1989.
sig: The principal historic fort of Sur, a major Omani seafaring town.
ex: Ministry of Heritage and Tourism (Experience Oman)
disc: Four towers: three round, one square
refs: Ministry of Heritage and Tourism. Al-Sunaysla Fort. Experience Oman. https://experienceoman.om/destinations/al-sharqiyah-south/al-sunaysla-fort
conf: Coordinates are the centre of the map bounding box embedded on the Ministry’s Experience Oman page (≈100 m); builder differs between accounts; the page’s ‘main structure about 35 m high’ is not used because it seems inconsistent with 5 m walls

s: 16th-century castle at Arabia’s easternmost point · teak ceilings from India
dr: Construction began in the 16th century; restored 1989 and 2008
el: Walls nearly 3 m thick; inner citadel over 13 m high
te: The castle where the sun rises first
se: At Ras Al Hadd, a stone castle guards the entrance of Khor Al-Hajar where the Sea of Oman meets the Arabian Sea
sa: في رأس الحد يحرس حصن حجري مدخل خور الحجر حيث يلتقي بحر عُمان ببحر العرب
desc: A castle in Ras Al Hadd, Wilayat of Sur, about 35 km from the town centre, on a plateau overlooking the entrance of Khor Al-Hajar at the meeting of the Sea of Oman and the Arabian Sea. Construction began in the 16th century with the participation of local tribes, and it served as a defensive centre and a place for tribal councils. Built of stone and gypsum, it has a main citadel and two towers linked by a wall nearly 3 m thick, a masabba for pouring hot liquids on attackers, cannons in the western tower and an inner citadel over 13 m high. Its ceilings use teak from India and timber from Mombasa and Zanzibar, and a passage of about 500 m is reported to lead to the Bir Marfas well; it was restored in 1989 and 2008.
sig: A coastal stronghold whose timbers record Oman’s Indian Ocean trade links.
ex: Ministry of Heritage and Tourism (Experience Oman)
disc: Teak from India in the ceilings
refs: Ministry of Heritage and Tourism. Ras Al Hadd Castle. Experience Oman. https://experienceoman.om/destinations/al-sharqiyah-south/ras-al-hadd-castle
conf: Coordinates are the centre of the map bounding box embedded on the Ministry’s Experience Oman page (≈100 m); about 1 km from the existing Ras al Hadd Turtle Reserve point, but a separate historic building

na: كهف مقل في وادي بني خالد
s: Karst cave with an underground river above the pools of Wadi Bani Khalid
dr: Solution cave with ceiling boreholes attributed to hypogene speleogenesis; not dated
el: Cave river flows even in dry periods
se: Beyond the green pools of Wadi Bani Khalid, a low cave leads down to a river that never stops running
sa: خلف برك وادي بني خالد الخضراء يقود كهف منخفض إلى نهر لا يتوقف عن الجريان
desc: A karst cave in Wadi Bani Khalid, Ash Sharqiyah North, reached by a trail of about 500 m from a restaurant beside the wadi’s natural pools. Its passages are mostly wide and low, with one chamber high enough to stand in and a crawl descending at about 30° to a cave river that runs strongly even in dry periods. Almost circular vertical boreholes in the ceiling are attributed to hypogene speleogenesis, and the rear has wet sections with cave clay; a second, higher entrance is a vertical shaft. The cave likely floods during wadi floods.
sig: Shows the groundwater system that feeds the perennial pools of Wadi Bani Khalid.
refs: Duckeck, J. Moqal Cave (مغارة مقل), Oman. Showcaves.com. https://showcaves.com/english/om/caves/Moqal.html
conf: Coordinates from Showcaves.com; timeline is a broad Quaternary estimate because the cave is not dated; Showcaves gives the Arabic name as مغارة مقل

s: Walled old quarter with fort, watchtowers and falaj in a ring of ophiolite hills · Al Qabil
dr: Documented for the Ministry of Heritage and Culture in a 2014 heritage management plan
el: Settlement core overlooked by Hisn al-Mudayrib
se: Near Al Qabil, mud-and-stone houses, watchtowers and an old fort hide inside a ring of dark hills
sa: قرب القابل تختبئ بيوت من الطين والحجر وأبراج مراقبة وحصن قديم داخل حلقة من التلال الداكنة
desc: An old settlement in the Al Qabil area of Ash Sharqiyah North, set as a single core within a ring of low ophiolite hills and overlooked by Hisn al-Mudayrib, an enclosure-type fort. It was surveyed by ArCHIAM for the Ministry of Heritage and Culture, with a documentation and heritage management plan completed in 2014 that also covers its falaj channels and bathing structures. Watchtowers linked by walls crown the surrounding hills; villagers say they were built during the period of Portuguese incursions. Many houses belonged to sheikhs and have private wells, and the village is home to the Al Harthy tribe.
sig: A well-documented example of a fortified Sharqiyah oasis quarter with its towers and falaj.
refs: ArCHIAM. Documentation and Heritage Management Plan: Harat al-Mudayrib, Al Qabil (2014). https://www.archiam.co.uk/documentation-and-heritage-management-plan-harat-al-mudayrib-al-qabil/
Oman Observer (6 November 2022). Walking through the ancient alleys of Al Mudhairib. https://www.omanobserver.om/ampArticle/1128004
conf: Coordinates from the ArCHIAM project page (22°36′51.06″N 58°40′34.11″E). No construction date is published; the timeline start (about AD 1600) is a broad estimate from the villagers’ attribution of the towers to the Portuguese period

n: Old quarters of Sinaw (Harat Al Barashid and Harat as-Sawafah)
s: About 300-year-old mud-and-stone quarters beside Sinaw’s famous souq
dr: Quarters about 300 years old (2022); documented in a 2014 heritage management plan
el: Two neighbouring harats in one master plan
te: The town of the desert market
se: Beside the market where Bedouin and fishermen trade, old houses with carved doors stand in the Sinaw oasis
sa: بجوار السوق الذي يلتقي فيه البدو والصيادون تقف بيوت قديمة بأبواب منقوشة في واحة سناو
desc: Harat Al Barashid and Harat as-Sawafah are neighbouring old quarters in the Sinaw oasis, Ash Sharqiyah North, documented by ArCHIAM for the Ministry of Heritage and Culture after a survey in autumn 2013, with a joint heritage management plan completed in 2014. Sinaw’s old quarters, described in 2022 as about 300 years old, contain mosques, traditional souqs, Qur’an schools and castles with high round towers, built of stone and clay with massive columns, decorated doors and arches. The traditional souq has four gates and remains a trading place where Bedouin and coastal fishermen sell their products. Many roofs have collapsed and the quarters are largely abandoned.
sig: Historic quarters of one of the main market towns between the Hajar mountains and the Sharqiyah desert.
refs: ArCHIAM. Documentation and Heritage Management Plan: Harat Al Barashid and Harat as-Sawafah, Sinaw Oasis (2014). https://archiam.co.uk/documentation-and-heritage-management-plan-harat-al-barashid-and-harat-as-sawafah-sinaw-oasis
Oman Observer (21 September 2022). Sinaw the cradle of Omani architecture. https://www.omanobserver.om/ampArticle/1125594
Oman Observer (13 December 2017). Old districts in Sinaw cry for care. https://www.omanobserver.om/ampArticle/66811
conf: Coordinates from the ArCHIAM project page (22°29′55.93″N 58°01′14.70″E). The 300-year age is from a 2022 newspaper; a 2017 article says many quarters date from the early 20th century. Arabic harat names are transliterations

s: Tidal inlet near Al Kahil with flamingos and wintering shorebirds · Key Biodiversity Area
se: On the Al Wusta coast, a long tidal lagoon fills with flamingos, spoonbills and thousands of sandpipers in winter
sa: على ساحل الوسطى تمتلئ بحيرة مدّ طويلة في الشتاء بطيور النحام وأبي ملعقة وآلاف الطيور الخواضة
desc: A tidal inlet about 6 km long near the township of Al Kahil on the Al Wusta coast, recognised as a Key Biodiversity Area covering about 6.07 km². Counts include 3,000 curlew sandpipers (Calidris ferruginea) in December, 1,500 greater flamingos in November, up to 110 Eurasian spoonbills, 234 ruddy turnstones, 104 pied avocets and 21 ospreys in February. The site lies within the proposed South Jazir National Nature Reserve of 18,000 ha. The Ministry of Heritage and Tourism describes it as a tidal lagoon with white dunes about 6 km east of Al Kahil.
sig: A key wintering and passage wetland for waterbirds on Oman’s central Arabian Sea coast.
refs: KBA Partnership. Khawr Ghawi (KBA 8237). Key Biodiversity Areas factsheet. https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/site/factsheet/8237
Ministry of Heritage and Tourism. Al Wusta visitor guide. https://experienceoman.om/media/huscq4j4/al-wusta-en.pdf
conf: Coordinates are the published KBA centre point; t0 counts from the 1994 assessment; flamingo listed as Phoenicopterus ruber in the factsheet

s: Mudflats and bay at Duqm with 3,000 flamingos and 77 bird species · Key Biodiversity Area
dr: Key Biodiversity Area (criteria A1b, D1a); last assessed 1994
te: Flamingos at the new port town
ta: طيور النحام في مدينة الميناء الجديدة
se: Beside the fast-growing port of Duqm, a sandy bay and mudflats feed thousands of flamingos every winter
sa: بجوار ميناء الدقم المتنامي يقدّم خليج رملي ومسطحات طينية الغذاء لآلاف طيور النحام كل شتاء
desc: A coastal Key Biodiversity Area of about 14.31 km² near the town of Ad Duqm on the bay of Ghubbat Quwayrat, Al Wusta. A total of 77 bird species has been recorded, with wintering counts of 3,000 greater flamingos, 212 Eurasian spoonbills in February, 175 pied avocets, 31 ospreys and 30 great egrets. It qualifies under global KBA criteria A1b and D1a, but only about 5% of the area is protected. The Ministry of Heritage and Tourism notes that the muddy flats beside Duqm’s 5-km beach attract sandpipers, plovers, avocets and greater flamingos.
sig: An important waterbird site now beside one of Oman’s largest development zones.
refs: KBA Partnership. Duqm (KBA 8234). Key Biodiversity Areas factsheet. https://www.keybiodiversityareas.org/site/factsheet/8234
Ministry of Heritage and Tourism. Al Wusta visitor guide. https://experienceoman.om/media/huscq4j4/al-wusta-en.pdf
conf: Coordinates are the published KBA centre point; about 1.9 km from the existing Duqm Rock Garden point, which is a geological record; t0 counts from the 1994 assessment; the name ‘Ghubbat Quwayrat’ is from the factsheet

s: Ediacaran stromatolite reefs and lagoons of the Huqf · recovery after the Shuram excursion
dr: Buah Formation, Nafun Group (about 645–547 Ma), Huqf Supergroup
el: Section BD1 spans 106.6 m of strata
se: In the Huqf desert, rocks more than 550 million years old preserve reefs and lagoons built by microbial mats
sa: في صحراء الحقف تحفظ صخور يزيد عمرها على 550 مليون عام شعابًا وبحيرات ضحلة بنتها حصائر ميكروبية
desc: Buah Dome in the Huqf area exposes the Buah Formation, a late Precambrian carbonate platform of the Nafun Group (about 645–547 Ma) in the Huqf Supergroup. Bergmann (2013) logged sections BD1–BD4 here and at nearby Mukhaibah Dome, describing reef facies of large domal and columnar stromatolites, Conophyton stromatolites in lagoons, oolitic shoals and evaporite pseudomorphs in peritidal beds. Carbon isotopes, which fall to about −12‰ in the underlying Shuram Formation, recover through the Buah from about −8‰ to about 0‰ and above. A positive excursion in the upper Buah is correlated with the Nama Group dated at 548.8 ± 1 Ma.
sig: A reference platform for how the carbon cycle recovered after the Shuram excursion, just before the first skeletal animals of the Ara Group.
refs: Bergmann, K.D. (2013). Constraints on the Carbon Cycle and Climate During the Early Evolution of Animals. PhD thesis, California Institute of Technology. Chapter 5 and Appendix C. https://doi.org/10.7907/KFJX-7S28
conf: Coordinates are the base of section BD1 in Bergmann (2013), Table C.1; timeline is an estimate within the 645–547 Ma Nafun Group range for the post-Shuram Buah interval, not a direct date; Arabic spelling of Buah is a transliteration. About 37 km from the existing Wadi Shuram point
